summary: Usage sampling window shift causes misattributed route-level billing and suppressed alerts
description: Beacon HealthTech reports that console usage rollups for several routes are being attributed to adjacent routes (route IDs shifted) and several anomaly alerts did not fire during a traffic spike on 2026-03-09. The issue appears correlated with usage sampling/rollup windows for high-cardinality routes in prod/us-east. Customer is on Dedicated tier; they see incorrect per-route billing on their invoice draft.
impact: Billing attributions for a subset (~2% of total tokens) of Beacon's March invoices are incorrect; 3 anomaly alerts (route-level throughput) failed to trigger during a customer-facing load spike causing delayed response. Affects downstream finance and on-call paging for customers using route-level thresholds.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In Beacon tenant (org ID: beacon-998), export 'per-route hourly usage' from Console for 2026-03-09 02:00-06:00 UTC.
2) Compare exported route_id column with raw ingestion events in ClickHouse table 'usage_events_v2' for same time window.
3) Query console alert evaluation logs for alerts 'beacon-route-peak-1', 'beacon-route-peak-2' in Alerting service for 2026-03-09.
4) Re-run hourly rollup job for that window (simulated) and observe route_id mapping changes after compaction step.
5) Observe that exported rollup rows have route_id values shifted by a deterministic offset for high-cardinality routes.
expected_result: Per-route usage exports and console rollups match raw ingestion events and alert evaluations trigger consistently on the same route identifiers.
actual_result: Some high-cardinality routes have their usage attributed to different route IDs after the hourly rollup/compaction job; alerting evaluation sampled a different set of route buckets and suppressed alerts for the true hot route.
logs: 2026-03-09T02:15:12Z alert-eval: beacon-route-peak-1 evaluated routes=1024 sampled=512 -> result=NO_ALERT
2026-03-09T02:16:30Z usage-ingest: event route_id=route-17 token_count=1245 received=2026-03-09T02:09:55Z partition=us-east-01
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: sampling window drift during compaction caused route-bucket boundary misalignment for high-cardinality routes.
Observed an unexpected 300s sampling_window_offset being applied in the hourly rollup logs (should be 0s). Offset only seen on us-east workers during a rolling config rollout.

Alert evaluation uses the same rollup buckets; when sampling window is offset, sampled route list differs and high-traffic route fell into a different evaluation bucket and was dropped by sampling threshold.
Cross-referenced with SUP-9642 (usage-export-mismatch) which had a separate compaction-time bug but not identical; linked for context.
Temporary repro in staging: toggling 'enable_rollup_offset' feature flag causes deterministic shift; flag was flipped in canary earlier on 2026-03-08 and rolled to us-east canary pool.
Related PR identified that introduced the offset calculation: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4256 (compaction scheduler change).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer reported invoice draft shows route-17 usage attributed to route-18 and their alerts did not page. Customer requests immediate mitigation and corrected draft.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Marco Diaz (SRE): Reproduced export mismatch in prod replica. Observed sampling_window_offset=300s in hourly rollup logs. Added logs to ticket and escalated to infra team. Pinged #support and #infra-rollouts.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Priya Mehta (Infra): Identified that canary config flip for feature 'rollup-window-offset' was accidentally enabled in us-east during rollout PR 4256. Rollback approved; preparing hotfix PR.

2026-03-11 02:05 - Marco Diaz (SRE): Applied immediate mitigation: disabled 'enable_rollup_offset' in production canary pool and requeued hourly rollup for affected windows (2026-03-09 00:00-06:00). Notified customer and finance to regenerate draft invoice.

2026-03-12 08:17 - Customer (Beacon Support Rep): Confirmed corrected invoice draft matches expected per-route usage; alert firing behavior observed to be restored for test spike. Awaiting final postmortem and permanent fix timeline.
resolution: Workaround: rolled back the canary config for 'rollup-window-offset' and reprocessed hourly rollups for affected windows. Customer invoice draft corrected. A permanent fix scheduled (see PR 4271).
resolution_notes: Root cause: a feature flag flip during a config rollout caused compaction logic to apply a non-zero sampling window offset on a subset of us-east workers. This offset changed how high-cardinality route buckets were sampled and later rolled up, leading to misattribution and alert sampling differences. Fix: revert offset behavior and add invariant tests for rollup bucket idempotency. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4271. Postmortem doc placeholder: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/67890-rollup-offset-incident.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add rollout guard to prevent feature flag flips from being included in production canary without automated integration test (owner: Priya Mehta).
2) Create regression test to assert rollup idempotency for N-minute offsets (owner: infra/rollup-team).
3) Schedule billing reconciliation call with Beacon finance and account team to correct prior draft invoices if needed (owner: CS reps).
4) Publish short postmortem and communicate SLAs impacted and credit plan if confirmed billing discrepancy persists (owner: ops).
